title: Motile designs spontaneously aggregate particles in simulation and in vivo

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Motile designs spontaneously aggregate particles in simulation and in vivo

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: When the environment contains particulate matter, motile designs spontaneously gather the particles into aggregates, both in simulation and as living Xenopus-cell organisms.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Results › Object Manipulation.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: When the environment is strewn with particulate matter, motile designs spontaneously aggregate the external objects both in silico (SI Appendix, Fig. S10) and in vivo (Fig. 3F and SI Appendix, Fig. S11).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J, “A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms”, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (2020), doi:10.1073/pnas.1910837117; section “Results › Object Manipulation.”. Scope: Xenopus reconfigurable organisms and their simulated counterparts in a particle-strewn dish

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2020-xenobots-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.70

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Particle aggregation is directly measurable in both systems. Public supplementary evidence can establish the demonstrated cases, while limited controls and uncertain raw-video availability constrain a full test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify particle-cluster number, size, and spatial concentration over time in simulation and video, comparing motile designs with immotile or shuffled-motion controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Aggregation can arise passively from flow and boundary effects.

Public material may provide videos but not all source frames or particle coordinates.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.82
discriminating power: 0.78
operationalizability: 0.95
data adequacy: 0.48
data existence: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Aggregation is measurable as particle clustering, and the simulator can be extended or re-run for the in silico half. The living half is a qualitative supplementary observation. Without non-motile controls, piled debris is also what any crawler would leave behind, so the result is only partly discriminating.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Place particles in the simulated dish and measure cluster size or particles gathered per time for motile designs versus non-motile controls; the same contrast on living builds would test the in vivo clause.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Passive sweeping by any moving object can pile particles up without a design-specific behavior.

Living aggregation is documented in figures and video, not as deposited particle tracks.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.4
analysis feasibility: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.75
data existence: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.5
